title: format-on-save runs `nvs fmt`, then the editor's own HTML formatter over each markup chunk, starting at the Novis block's indentation
scope:
what a format request in an editor does to a `.nvs` file with inline HTML in it, and the
one layout rule `nvs fmt` gains so the two halves meet. It changes nothing else `nvs fmt` does, and it
does not decide how the PhpStorm client formats markup.

summary.headline: Format-on-save formats the HTML too, indented from the code that opened it
summary.body:
Saving a `.nvs` file runs `nvs fmt` over the whole file, asks the compiler where the markup
regions are, and then runs the editor's own HTML formatter over each region, starting at the
indentation of the `?>` line that opened it. `nvs fmt` gains one rule to make that work: a `?>`
that begins its line sits at the depth of the block it is in. Markup therefore indents from
where the code is, so a file no longer jumps between the two. The pass is on by default and
`nvs.template.format` turns it off.
